key_insight: Thermally sprayed Inconel 625 is a durable alternative to Pyromark 2500 for GEN3 solar receivers, retaining ~93% solar absorptivity after 10,000 thermal cycles.
engineering_relevance: At 800 °C, Inconel 625 coatings offer lower emissivity and modeled energy costs than Pyromark, supporting high-temperature receiver designs with reduced maintenance needs.
method: Deposit Inconel 625 by compact plasma spraying; pre-treat for 8 or 168 h at 800 °C.
Apply 10,000 accelerated thermal cycles at 750 °C; assess optical properties, microstructure and coating integrity.
Compare levelized coating and energy costs with Pyromark 2500.
evidence_signal: After cycling, Inconel 625 showed no delamination and 70–86% emissivity versus Pyromark’s 83–96%; modeled LCOE at 800 °C was $45.89–46.48/MWh versus $48.78/MWh.
watch_item: Cycling was performed at 750 °C, so long-term durability under full receiver operating conditions at 800 °C still requires validation.
paper_title: Performance assessment of thermally sprayed Inconel 625 coatings as an alternative for next-generation central tower solar receivers
